column3: Behold introduces the tears, and the oppressors’ hand is singular.
Skill in the work is named rather than simply success.
Returning and seeing are separately expressed.
The eye is singular. The first description explicitly says one and no second.
The first condition is if they fall, with a plural subject, rather than if one falls.
The two stand against him, with the opponent explicitly expressed.
The youth is not explicitly repeated as the subject; coming out of prison and being born are completed actions.
The living are with the second youth; followed is not an expressed verb.
The latter people will not rejoice in him, rather than a passive statement that the successor will not be celebrated.
